user_query: What happens if the total games are tied when time expires in a USTA timed match?
right_answer: If total games are tied when time expires, many USTA timed match procedures require a single deciding or sudden-death point to determine the winner, depending on the local league rules.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: If score is tied, play one deciding point.

must_not_include: match automatically ends in a tie

user_query: Time runs out right after I hit a winner but before it lands. Does the point count?
right_answer: Yes. The point must be completed if it was already in progress when time expired. The result of that point counts once it finishes.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: A point in play as the timer goes off should be finished.

user_query: I hit a ball that my opponent clearly could not reach, but I accidentally shouted during the shot. Do I lose the point?
right_answer: It depends on whether the hindrance was intentional. If the shout was unintentional, the point is replayed as a let. If it was deliberate and hindered the opponent, you lose the point.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: Deliberate hindrance: opponent wins the point. Unintentional hindrance: replay the point.

user_query: My opponent hit a ball that landed just out, but I returned it anyway. Can I still call it out after I hit it?
right_answer: No. A player must make calls promptly. If you return the ball, you are generally considered to have accepted it as good and cannot later call it out.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: Calls must be made promptly; delay implies acceptance.

user_query: In a timed USTA league match, the total games are tied when time runs out. Who wins?
right_answer: It depends on the local league rules. In many USTA timed match formats, including PNW, a single deciding or sudden-death point is played to determine the winner rather than ending in a tie.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: If score is tied, play one deciding point.

user_query: We realized after 3 games that we started on the wrong sides of the court. Do we restart the match?
right_answer: No. Points already played stand. Players correct the positions going forward, but the match does not restart.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: Errors are corrected as soon as discovered; previous points stand.

user_query: In a tiebreak, we discover the wrong player has been serving after an even number of points. What happens?
right_answer: If discovered after an even number of points, the service order is corrected immediately.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: If discovered after an even number of points, correct immediately.

user_query: A ball was 99% out but I wasn't completely sure. Can I call it out?
right_answer: No. If you are not certain the ball is out, it must be called good. The opponent gets the benefit of the doubt.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: Any doubt must be resolved in favor of the opponent.

user_query: My opponent’s hat fell off during a point and distracted me. Do I win the point?
right_answer: No. This is generally treated as unintentional hindrance. A let may be played if it affected the point, but it is not an automatic loss of point.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: Unintentional hindrance results in replay of the point.

user_query: Can spectators tell me if a ball was in or out during a match?
right_answer: No. Spectators are not allowed to make or assist with line calls. Players are responsible for calls on their side of the court.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: Spectators have no role in making calls.

user_query: A let is called after my first serve fault because a ball rolled onto the court. Do I get a first or second serve?
right_answer: You get a first serve. When a let is called due to outside interference, the entire point is replayed, so previous faults are canceled.

evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: When a let is called, the whole point is replayed.
